environment: three coordinator processes on localhost, no Docker, no database

checks.name: cluster forms with a leader and quorum
fair_share is committed on its own once every peer supports it
the policy endpoint refuses a missing or wrong admin token
first_come lets one building hold 102 A while the others get 7 A and 4 A
fair_share moves a hog (102/7/4 A) to the max-min shares (40 A each)
a changed demand mix (10/100/100 A) converges to 10/55/55 A
a new leader is elected within a bound after the leader is killed
grants continue under the new leader and the shares hold
the restarted node rejoins and every replica ends in the same state
the granted total never exceeded the capacity on any live node

limits: Sampling about twice a second is evidence, not a proof.
One run on one machine; the processes share a clock and a loopback network.
No gateways, MQTT, PostgreSQL, nginx or control service: those are covered by their own tests and the Docker evaluation.
